diagnosis.narrative: The trial shows a retrieval-dominated failure pattern with 82% of failures attributable to retrieval. The shift from hybrid to vector-only retrieval dramatically improved retrieval completeness (complete rate up from 0.35 to 0.432, acc_given_complete up from 0.77 to 0.921), but introduced a new problem: ranking fragility for multi-hop questions. The 8.9% partial retrieval rate (trial 1) has ballooned to 48.9%, indicating that while the retriever finds more relevant documents, it fails to surface both required spans within top-20. This manifests as rampant refusals (6% rate) when the model sees only one side of a comparison or inference question. Deep inspection reveals systematic ranking degradation: in multi-doc questions, the second span often appears at ranks 11-19 (e.g., mhrag_1621 span at rank 12, mhrag_425 span at rank 11, mhrag_1318 span at rank 19). Meanwhile, pure retrieval_miss persists at 8% on questions requiring entity disambiguation (mhrag_409: 'Federal Reserve' vs hallucinated 'Reserve Bank of Australia') or highly specific document targeting (mhrag_1422, mhrag_938). The generation failures that do occur (3/17) cluster on negation handling and comparative reasoning even when context is complete (mhrag_1444, mhrag_1127). The removal of reranking (bge-reranker-v2-m3 → none, top_n 8→3) and query expansion (decompose → none) appears to have traded recall-oriented hybrid search for precision-oriented dense search, sacrificing composition of multi-hop evidence.
